title: Associated points of flat pullback over a locally Noetherian scheme
statement:
Let $h:Y\to Z$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], with $Z$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\mathcal G$ be any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For a module $\mathcal H$ on a scheme $W$, write $\operatorname{Ass}_W(\mathcal H)$ for the points whose stalk maximal ideal is the annihilator of an element of $\mathcal H_w$, as in [def-trf-relative-assassin]. For $z\in Z$, let $Y_z$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $j_z:Y_z\to Y$ its projection. Then, as subsets of $Y$,
$$\operatorname{Ass}_Y(h^*\mathcal G)=\bigcup_{z\in\operatorname{Ass}_Z(\mathcal G)}j_z\bigl(\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_z}(\mathcal O_{Y_z})\bigr).$$
Here $h^*$ is pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. No finite-type hypothesis on $\mathcal G$, and no local Noetherianity hypothesis on $Y$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05DB (lemma-bourbaki), equality for a locally Noetherian base, specialized to the relatively flat sheaf O_Y; O_Y tensor h^*G = h^*G.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$ and put $z=h(y)$, $A=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $M=\mathcal G_z$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$. The stalk homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ is local and $B$ is flat over $A$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood of $z$ from [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), $A$ is a prime localization of its coordinate ring; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $A$ Noetherian. No assertion about Noetherianity of $B$ or finiteness of $M$ has been made.

source.place: Tag 05DB (lemma-bourbaki), proof: set A, B, M and specialize F=O_Y

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback], $(h^*\mathcal G)_y\cong M\otimes_A B$ as $B$-modules. An isomorphism preserves the annihilator of each element, so [def-trf-relative-assassin] identifies $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_Y(h^*\mathcal G)$ with $\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B)$, always using exact element-annihilators. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], the unique point $y_z$ of $Y_z$ above $y$ has local ring $C=B/\mathfrak m_A B$, compatibly with the quotient map. Since $\varphi$ is local, $\mathfrak m_A B\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, and the maximal ideal of $C$ is $\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_A B$. Thus the fibre association condition is that this ideal is the annihilator of an element of $C$.

source.place: Tag 05DB, proof: stalk of pullback and local ring of fibre; Schemes Tag 0HA1

proof.text:
Apply the equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-flat-base-change] with $R=A$, $S=B$, and $N=B$. Step 1 verifies both hypotheses, and its statement allows arbitrary $M$ and arbitrary $B$. Hence
$$\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{there is }\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)\text{ with }\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(B/\mathfrak pB).$$
We next identify which $\mathfrak p$ can occur, rather than assuming it equals $\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Tag 05DB via Algebra Tag 05C2 (lemma-bourbaki-fibres); expand its reference to Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki)

proof.text: Suppose $\mathfrak m_B=\operatorname{Ann}_B(v)$ for $v\in B/\mathfrak pB$, where $\mathfrak p$ is prime in $A$. The element $v$ is nonzero because $\mathfrak m_B$ is proper. For $a\notin\mathfrak p$, multiplication by $a$ on $A/\mathfrak p$ is injective: $ar\in\mathfrak p$ implies $r\in\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring this injection with the $A$-flat module $B$ stays injective. The isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring](1) identifies the tensor module with $B/\mathfrak pB$ by $\bar r\otimes b\mapsto\varphi(r)b$; on these generators the tensor map is multiplication by $\varphi(a)$. Consequently $\varphi(a)$ cannot annihilate $v$. If $a\in\mathfrak m_A\setminus\mathfrak p$, locality gives $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m_B$, contradicting this conclusion. Hence $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Every proper ideal of the local ring $A$ is contained in $\mathfrak m_A$ (each element outside it is a unit), so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Algebra Tags 0312 and 05C1 (lemma-post-bourbaki), nonzerodivisor calculation on the prime quotient; used in 05C2

proof.text:
For $C=B/\mathfrak m_A B$ and $v\in C$, the $B$-annihilator is the inverse image of the $C$-annihilator under the surjection $B\to C$. Therefore
$$\operatorname{Ann}_B(v)=\mathfrak m_B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Ann}_C(v)=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_A B.$$
Indeed the preimage of the displayed quotient ideal is $\mathfrak m_B$, and surjectivity makes ideals of $C$ equal when their preimages are equal. By the definition [def-trf-relative-assassin] and step 2, this proves
$$\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(B/\mathfrak m_A B)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y_z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_z}(\mathcal O_{Y_z}).$$
It holds even if $B$ and $C$ are non-Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05DB, proof: closed-fibre association; Algebra Tag 05BY (lemma-ass-quotient-ring), direct annihilator calculation

proof.text:
Steps 3–5 give the equivalence
$$\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\mathfrak m_A\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)\text{ and }y_z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_z}(\mathcal O_{Y_z})\bigr).$$
For the forward implication choose $\mathfrak p$ in step 3, identify it by step 4, and apply step 5. For the reverse implication use step 5 and take $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$ in step 3. By [def-trf-relative-assassin], the first condition on the right is exactly $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_Z(\mathcal G)$. Step 2 identifies the left condition with association of $y$ to $h^*\mathcal G$. Finally [def-pc-scheme-fibre] says $j_z$ identifies the points of $Y_z$ with $h^{-1}(z)$. Thus a fixed $y$ lies in the union in the statement precisely when these two right-hand conditions hold for $z=h(y)$. Since this holds for every $y$, the required equality of subsets follows.

source.place: Tag 05DB, conclusion of the stalkwise equivalence

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-7a740c49e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six steps in full; the delivery adds no new nodes. The statement is Stacks divisors 05DB (l.311) taken with F=O_Y and checked against its stalkwise proof: equality needs only Z locally Noetherian, G stays any quasi-coherent module and Y need not be Noetherian, so it is not weakened. Step 1: the flat-morphism definition gives the local stalk map, and the locnoeth definition, clause (c) of affine-open-stalk-localization and localization-noetherian make A Noetherian. Step 2: module-stalk-pullback holds for any module, and fibre-stalk-quotient (0HA1) gives O_{Y_z,y_z}=B/m_A B. Step 3: the 0312 node (algebra.tex l.15774) allows any M and S with N flat, applied with R=A and S=N=B. Step 4: I checked the argument that p=m_A: injectivity of multiplication by a on A/p carries over to B/pB by flat-tensor-exact and part (1) of tensor-over-quotient, and locality then forces m_A⊆p. Step 5 is the elementary annihilator correspondence along B→C. Step 6 uses that j_z maps onto h^{-1}(z). Small cases hold: A^1 over k[[t]] with G=O_Z or G=k, G=0, Y empty, h=id, and Z=Spec k with Y non-Noetherian. There is no duplicate: the related nodes need Noetherian rings and finite modules, or finite presentation with WeakAss. The proof closure (79 nodes) has no cycle. I accept the three declared tool_uses (module-stalk-pullback, scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient, the 0312 node) as generic black boxes. No SGA is cited.
